questions.explain: The chapter states the rule explicitly: never let both layers tune the same knob. If the platform owns plan forcing, the ADE's plan-forcing agent must defer, and the division must be enforced in the action dispatcher.
options: The ADE should always override platform decisions
Never let both layers tune the same knob
The platform should be disabled wherever the ADE runs
Both layers should tune indexes for redundancy
questions.q: What is the chapter's central coordination rule between the Azure SQL platform control plane and the ADE?

questions.explain: A serverless database can be paused; connecting to it triggers auto-resume taking 30-60 seconds, and a naive health check will report it as down during that window. Agents must check state first and distinguish paused from down.
options: DMVs are disabled on serverless databases
A connection attempt to a paused database triggers auto-resume (30-60 s), so a naive check reports the database as down during resume
The control plane view is required for billing
Data-plane connections are blocked by the firewall
questions.q: According to the chapter, why must ADE health checks query the control plane's view of database state before opening a data-plane connection to a serverless database?

questions.explain: Two failover authorities — the platform and the ADE agent — will eventually disagree about whether a failover is warranted, producing a failover war between regions. Availability for failover-group members is platform-managed.
options: Failover groups do not support read-only listeners
The platform already pages the on-call engineer
Two failover authorities will eventually disagree, causing a failover war that ping-pongs the database between regions
ADE failover agents cannot read sys.databases
questions.q: Why must the ADE's own failover agents be disabled for databases in an automatic failover group?

questions.explain: The chapter recommends letting the platform own automatic plan correction while the ADE owns index management, or vice versa, but the choice must be documented and enforced — never duplicated on both sides.
options: Let the platform own automatic plan correction and the ADE own index management, or vice versa — but document and enforce the choice
Always enable all three automatic tuning options and duplicate them in the ADE
Disable plan correction and let the ADE force all plans
Leave automatic tuning entirely to the DBA's manual judgment
questions.q: What is the recommended division of labor between Azure SQL automatic tuning and the ADE, per the chapter?

questions.explain: The chapter uses sys.dm_db_tuning_recommendations (reason, score, implementation script, state, timestamps) as the observation surface, and recommends ingesting its history into the ADE's action log.
options: sys.dm_exec_requests
sys.dm_db_tuning_recommendations
sys.dm_os_performance_counters
sys.database_automatic_tuning_options
questions.q: Which DMV does the chapter identify as the observation surface for what automatic tuning has done recently?
